subject: Packaging review: bundle unwind & tier-switch friction
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@medisync.io>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@medisync.io
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging review: bundle unwind & tier-switch friction

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking a look. We ran a usage audit and are seeing a steady drop in peak throughput over the last 6 weeks as a couple of teams reduce non-critical automation jobs. That said, feature usage (notably the semantic-search reranker and the policy-scoring outputs) remains critical for product.

We need to understand the operational impact and options if we move from our current Throughput-tier (T3) to a smaller footprint plan. The questions on our side are:

- If we downgrade tiers, which feature entitlements are tied to the tier vs. the seat count? Will customers lose access to the reranker immediately or only after a configuration change?
- Do you support a time-limited preservation of features during a step-down (e.g., keep entitlements for 60/90 days while throughput scales down)?
- Are prorated credits or feature-credit buckets an option instead of a full-tier downgrade?
- If we accept a quantized model (int8) on some workloads as a lower-cost variant, will Redwood guarantee parity SLAs for latency-sensitive calls?

Attached is a short usage export and our top-of-stack feature list for Q2. We have a renewal in 10 weeks and want to avoid a churny negotiation if we can map a safe downgrade path. Any proposals you can share would help our finance and product teams.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Platform
Medisync

[Attachment: current_usage_report_Q2.xlsx]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <priya@medisync.io>
Cc: ops@medisync.io
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging review: bundle unwind & tier-switch friction

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the context and the export. Short answer: we can create downgrade paths that avoid sudden feature loss, but there are trade-offs between product simplicity and operational overhead. Below are three pragmatic options you can review; I included a quick appendix as a PDF (tier-comparison-20270814.pdf).

Option A — Safe Step-down (default)
- Keep entitlements for core features (reranker, policy-scoring) for a 60-day grace window after a tier downgrade.
- After 60 days, entitlements are converted to a feature-credit bucket you can draw from.
- No immediate change to your calls; runtime will continue routing to the verified model variant.
- Implementation: small billing amendment + flag flip in 1 business day.

Option B — Throughput-first, credit buffer (recommended if you expect transient drops)
- Move to a lower throughput slab immediately but provision a monthly token credit buffer (equal to ~25% of your avg peak).
- Credits apply automatically to overflow.
- Feature entitlements remain, but latency SLOs on overflow will target the lower-cost quantized model (we'll notify and allow per-endpoint opt-outs).

Option C — Hybrid preservation (longer runway, more cost)
- Preserve full entitlements for 90 days and apply a time-limited discount on committed spend for that period.
- After 90 days, we either revert to Option A or you can elect a permanent conversion to a modular addon pricing for preserved features.

Pricing & discount note
- For customers doing a safety-first downgrade to avoid churn, we typically offer a short-term concession: 10–15% credit applied to the month of downgrade or a one-time invoice credit to offset migration work.
- If you commit to a 12-month smaller footprint with an annual prepay, we can extend a steeper discount (15%+) and guarantee a 90-day preservation window.

Operational considerations
- Option B increases runtime routing complexity; we recommend restricting auto-fallback to up to 3 critical endpoints to keep tracing and cost attribution simpler.
- Option C requires a short engineering change to add a per-feature entitlement flag; we can scope that in a 2-week engineering ticket if you want to standardize this across customers.

Next steps
1) If any of the options look promising, let's run a 30-minute workshop next week with your platform + finance to pick one.
2) I can draft an amendment (if you prefer) that shows the exact credit math and the DocuSign flow.

Attaching a one-pager comparing the three options.

Best,

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Packaging review: bundle unwind & tier-switch friction

Stephanie — looping in Karthik and Lauren with a suggested go-to. My read is Medisync wants minimal disruption and a clean credit path. Quick thoughts:

- Offer the 90-day preservation (Option C) but tie it to a short pilot surcharge that we apply as a refundable credit if they stay within a defined downgrade envelope. Keeps it low risk for us.
- Provide a single-line addon SKU called "Preserved Entitlements (90d)" so ops can easily apply/remove without deep engineering.
- Discount: 12% one-time invoice credit for the month of the downgrade + the refundable pilot credit.

Karthik — will this SKU be horrible to support? If yes, we default to Option A with a 60-day window and a small credit; if not, Option C + add-on SKU is my preference.

Lauren — I think CS should offer a migration playbook and a 1:1 runbook review with their SRE during the window.

-Ben

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the export and the clarity on timelines. After the internal review, here is a concrete proposal that balances operational simplicity with the preservation you asked for.

Proposal (final)
- 90-day Preservation Add-on ("Preserved Entitlements (90d)"): preserves reranker + policy-scoring entitlements for 90 days post-downgrade. After 90 days remaining credits convert to a feature-credit bucket.
- Pilot refundable buffer: 25% throughput credit buffer for the first month to cover transient overflow. This buffer is applied automatically and reconciled on the next invoice.
- Concession: one-time invoice credit equal to 12% of the month-of-downgrade spend.
- If Medisync commits to a 12-month agreement on the new tier within 30 days of amendment signature, Redwood will extend the preservation window to 120 days and increase the one-time credit to 15%.

Operational notes
- We will implement the add-on as an operations-applied SKU; no major code changes required. Karthik's team will provide the flag gating for two endpoints to ensure safe fallback.
- CS (Lauren) will run a migration playbook review with your SREs and share a checklist for tracing, sampling, and escalation.

Attached: a draft contract amendment and the tier comparison one-pager. If this looks good I can open a DocuSign envelope (linked below) and Ben will coordinate discounting on the invoice.

Next steps for Medisync
1) Confirm you want the 90-day preservation add-on + pilot buffer (reply to this thread).
2) If yes, I will send the amendment for signature and schedule the playbook call (30 min).

If you prefer a lighter-weight path we can default back to Option A (60-day grace + single invoice credit).

Best regards,
